text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"The US Institute of Medicine (now the National Academies) set a recommended dietary allowance of about 600 IU (15 micrograms) per day of vitamin D for adults up to age 70.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c2","text":"The recommended dietary allowance of vitamin D for adults older than 70 is about 800 IU per day.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Sun exposure for vitamin D production varies with latitude, season, skin pigmentation, and sunscreen use.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Older adults, housebound people, and those with darker skin may benefit from vitamin D supplementation.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c5","text":"People with malabsorption conditions such as Crohn's disease or celiac disease may benefit from vitamin D supplementation.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c6","text":"Excess vitamin D intake can cause hypercalcemia and kidney problems.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c7","text":"A blood test for 25-hydroxyvitamin D can be used to determine whether vitamin D supplementation is warranted.","cited_pids":[]}]}
